newsitem.title: FINLAND: Sampo leads Helsinki up, Raisio falls, Silja jumps.
newsitem.headline: Sampo leads Helsinki up, Raisio falls, Silja jumps.

text.p: Shares rose on Friday with trade turning lively in the afternoon after a dormant start, as underlying strong sentiment revived despite some nerves ahead of a U.S. Federal reserve meeting next week, brokers said.

The HEX index rose 0.42 percent to 2,139.1 with volume a fair 345 million markka. But this was about the extent of its performance on a week marked by hesitance and jitters about the potential pain of a rising markka.

Sampo was liveliest, hitting a two-year high to end up 10.50 markka at 314.50 and making up 20 percent of total volume, as brokers said falling interest rates boosted expectations of higher investment income for the group.
Silja jumped five markka to 37.00 on a late channel traffic announcement which was seen capping its losses in the UK.
Kemira set a new 53.20 life high on hopes its planned issue would pull a high price. Konecranes also set a new record on buying ahead of its results due next week, brokers said.

But Raision Tehtaat fell sharply -- down nine markka or over three percent to 271.00 -- after a story in the New York Times said U.S. Campbell Soup would begin selling by mail-order frozen meals designed to reduce high blood pressure, cholesterol and diabetes.
Brokers in Helsinki were slightly mystified but some sources said this had been interpreted as a potential threat to Raisio's patented cholesterol-lowering Benecol margarine.
